entries.clue: Frustrate fly (4)

blocks.note: as when hopes are thwarted or wrecked
fly in the sense of hurry off, not the insect

annotation.walkthrough: Two verbs side by side; 'fly' tempts you towards insects or trouser zips, but here it simply means hurry.
annotation.definitionFit: To dash someone's plans is to frustrate them, and to dash somewhere is to fly there.

entries.clue: Dad’s come up, popping in to contradict and censure (10)

indicatorNotes.come up: in a down entry, coming up means reading bottom to top
indicatorNotes.popping in to: the reversed piece pops inside the other word

blocks.note: PA = dad; come up (reversed) to AP
to prove wrong; opened up as DIS…PROVE to take AP

annotation.surface: Father has come upstairs and barged into an argument to tell someone off.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': Dad has come up, so PA turns to AP and slips into the word for contradict.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to censure is to express strong disapproval, covering both judging and reprimanding.

entries.clue: Summer clothing, blue: a brief distraction (5,5)

blocks.note: blue is the colour of the Conservative (Tory) party

annotation.surface: Someone in blue summer shorts is a passing distraction.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics blue is the Conservative colour, so 'blue' can stand for TORY. The definition is playful: a short story is a brief diversion from the day.
annotation.definitionFit: A short story is a brief piece of fiction, read as a short distraction.

entries.clue: Piano music, as can be picked up in Chinatown (10)

annotation.definition2: as can be picked up in Chinatown

blocks.note: a simple two-finger waltz every beginner learns

blocks.clueFragment: as can be picked up in Chinatown
blocks.note: eating sticks you pick up at a Chinese restaurant

annotation.surface: A tune you might hear, and learn, while wandering around Chinatown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' works twice: chopsticks are literally picked up at the table, and a tune is picked up by ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Chopsticks is a famous simple piano piece and also the utensils used in Chinese restaurants.

entries.clue: Harry’s getting drunk with us: cheers! (7)

annotation.definitionNote: an exclamation used as a plural noun: cheers = shouts of hurray

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk's letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: Harry is getting tipsy with the gang and raising a glass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' looks like a toast to go with the drinking, but it is the definition: shouts of approval.
annotation.definitionFit: As a plural noun, cheers are shouts of joy, and hurray is the word shouted, so the plural names those shouts.

entries.clue: Ingredients of tapas, satay and Italian sauce (7)

indicatorNotes.Ingredients of: the answer is made from what is inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A recipe list: bits of tapas, satay and an Italian sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The food surface keeps the hidden answer in its own kitchen; 'Ingredients' sounds culinary but means letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved tomato sauce used in Italian cooking.

entries.clue: Perfect scores (6-6)

blocks.note: a score is twenty, so two scores are twenty and twenty

annotation.surface: Full marks on a test.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like results, but a score is the old word for twenty; two of them make the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty describes perfect eyesight, and two scores written out are twenty twenty.

entries.clue: Canonically, Abel’s iniquitous nemesis, primarily? (4)

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the prime, first, letter of each word

annotation.surface: A Bible note: according to scripture, the wicked enemy of Abel.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the recipe and the description: in Genesis, Cain murdered his brother Abel.
annotation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Cain killed his brother Abel, making him Abel's wicked nemesis.

entries.clue: Band’s appeal? Not a sound (4)

annotation.surface: A music group's charm lies in not making noise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' pulls towards musicians and 'sound' supports that picture, but the band is a strip of cloth worn across the body.
annotation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of fabric worn around the waist or over a shoulder.

entries.clue: Diligent pupil trails back (4)

blocks.note: a car that tows another trails it behind

annotation.surface: A hard-working student lags behind.
annotation.walkthrough: A swot is British school slang for a pupil who studies very hard. 'Trails' here means pulls along, not falls behind.
annotation.definitionFit: A swot is a pupil who studies diligently.

entries.clue: Supports chain restaurants (10)

blocks.note: a chain of events is a series

annotation.surface: A business line: someone backs a group of chain restaurants.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chain restaurants' reads as one phrase, but 'chain' belongs to the wordplay and 'restaurants' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brasserie is a French-style informal restaurant, originally one attached to a brewery.

entries.clue: Party top substantial woman’s lost: turn around (2,1,3-6)

indicatorNotes.lost: the woman's W has gone missing from the word

annotation.surface: At a party, a large woman has lost her top and spins round.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 (written A ONE) means first-rate. The answer swings through 180 degrees, reversing direction.
annotation.definitionFit: To do a one-eighty is to turn around completely, reversing your position.

entries.clue: Does an impresario’s job – or just pretends (4,2,2,3)

blocks.note: someone pretending is putting on an act

annotation.surface: A showman staging acts, or perhaps only faking it.
annotation.walkthrough: The same phrase read literally (staging a show) and figuratively (faking a manner).
annotation.definitionFit: An impresario puts on acts for audiences; someone feigning puts on an act.

entries.clue: Interlaces ornately to bring everything to one place (10)

indicatorNotes.ornately: letters arranged elaborately, in a new pattern

annotation.surface: Weaving threads elaborately so that they all meet at one point.
annotation.walkthrough: The weaving picture fits the definition nicely: interlaced strands are drawn to a single centre.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition spells out the verb's meaning: gathering control or things at a single centre.

entries.clue: Country’s down on job that’s announced (5,5)

indicatorNotes.that’s announced: the job is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: south is down on a map

annotation.surface: A nation is fed up with its work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Down on' reads as disliking, but 'down' is the map direction SOUTH and 'on' just puts it before the job.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the East Asian nation below the Korean border is one country.

entries.clue: Speech’s missing opening – making allowances? (7)

blocks.note: orations are speeches; the 's makes it plural; lose the O

annotation.surface: A speech that lacks an opening, perhaps making excuses for itself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making allowances' reads as being forgiving; here allowances are fixed portions, such as wartime food rations.
annotation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of food or supplies.

entries.clue: Cordate, styled in ‘20s fashion (3,4)

indicatorNotes.styled: the letters are given a new style, an arrangement

annotation.surface: Something heart-shaped, designed in the manner of the 1920s.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Styled' and 'fashion' both sound like design talk, which lets the indicator hide in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Art Deco was the geometric design style of the 1920s and 1930s.

entries.clue: Artist’s questionable offering welcomed by deviate (7)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: taken in by, placed inside, the other word

blocks.note: to veer is to deviate; split V…EER

annotation.surface: A painter's dubious work is taken in by a deviant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offering' suggests an artwork, but it is just a sound offered in doubt: ERM, the noise of hesitation.
annotation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter.

entries.clue: Piece belonging to collector is Ottoman dish (7)

indicatorNotes.Piece belonging to: a piece of the following words holds the answer

annotation.surface: A collector owns an item that turns out to be a Turkish dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ottoman dish' looks like one phrase and suggests Turkish food, but 'Ottoman' only supplies letters; the dish is Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the creamy rice preparation of northern Italy is one kind of dish.

entries.clue: Announced what you may do to a flat singer (4-3)

indicatorNotes.Announced: said out, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.clueFragment: what you may do to a flat
blocks.note: you can rent out a flat

annotation.surface: Advice on what to do with a singer who keeps going flat.
annotation.walkthrough: A flat singer sounds like someone off key, but the flat is an apartment and the singer a songbird: the wrentit is a small North American bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The wrentit is a small songbird of the western United States.

entries.clue: Everyman would get stuck in to vacuous words and devices (7)

indicatorNotes.stuck in to: one piece is put inside the other
indicatorNotes.vacuous: empty, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: WORDS emptied of its middle: W…S
the setter, Everyman, is I; I would get = I'D GET

annotation.surface: The setter would get involved in empty talk and gadgets.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter referring to themselves by name stands for I. 'Would' shortens to 'D, as in I'd.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names small unspecified gadgets, as in a manufacturer's hypothetical product.

entries.clue: Certain kids jostled for favourable position (6,5)

indicatorNotes.jostled: pushed about, so the letters move

annotation.surface: Children pushing and shoving to get the best spot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a playground scramble, which is exactly what getting the inside track means.
annotation.definitionFit: The inside track is the shortest lane on a racecourse, hence an advantageous position.

entries.clue: With derisive remarks, sent up old king (4)

indicatorNotes.sent up: in a down entry, sending up reads the letters bottom to top

annotation.surface: An old monarch mocked and satirised with jeering comments.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' doubles as mocked, which suits the derisive remarks, but in a down clue it turns the letters upward.
annotation.definitionFit: Shah was the title of the kings of Persia (Iran).

entries.clue: End of U-boat? About time! (4)

indicatorNotes.About: around: one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a U-boat is a submarine, a sub

annotation.surface: The last moments of a U-boat, and not a moment too soon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of' looks like a letter-picking instruction for U-boat's last letter, but 'End' is the definition: a stub is a leftover end.
annotation.definitionFit: A stub is the end left over, as of a pencil or cigarette.

entries.clue: Devise alien people, ones who’ll do the dirty work (7,3)

annotation.definition: ones who’ll do the dirty work

blocks.note: to hatch a plan is to devise it

annotation.surface: Hatch a plot using foreigners to carry out the unpleasant jobs.
annotation.walkthrough: Hatchet men are hired to do ruthless or unpleasant tasks on someone's behalf.
annotation.definitionFit: Hatchet men carry out the dirty work, such as firings or attacks, for others.

entries.clue: Row when Mr Woods ditches golf (4)

indicatorNotes.ditches: gets rid of the named letter

blocks.note: G = golf in the NATO alphabet; removed from TIGER

annotation.surface: An argument breaks out when Tiger Woods quits the game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel in the surface, but it is a line of seats. Golf is G in the phonetic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the seating sense: stadium seats rise in rows, each one a level above the last.

entries.clue: What you do in spare time, finding charger: it’s an obsession (5,5)

blocks.clueFragment: What you do in spare time
blocks.note: a hobby is a spare-time pastime

annotation.surface: A pastime that becomes a fixation, like hunting for a phone charger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charger' sounds electrical, but it is the old word for a cavalry horse.
annotation.definitionFit: A hobby horse is a pet subject someone keeps returning to obsessively.

entries.clue: Wager on a character coming from Athens (4)

annotation.surface: Betting on a traveller arriving from Athens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: Beta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character from Athens.
